speaker: A
text: A: Well I'll start it off by saying I'm homeless folks.

speaker: A
text: I got kicked out of my Malibu place.

speaker: A
text: That's a clinic, you know, rehab for wealthy people, and they decided they wanted to make some changes on the property.

speaker: A
text: So they had to have a building inspector come over and approve the changes that they wanted to make.

speaker: A
text: So the building inspector decided to inspect everything on the property.

speaker: A
text: Came to my house and he said, there's no permit for this house, you've got to tear it down.

speaker: A
text: So I just got notice on Tuesday.

speaker: A
text: So everything is going into boxes.

speaker: A
text: So I'm homeless.

speaker: A
text: And they gave me until the 18th, but I'm leaving tomorrow for Thailand, so I had to pack up everything in five days.

text: Q: Do you have help?

speaker: A
text: A: No, I don't want any help because I want to know where exactly everything is.

speaker: A
text: Thank you.

speaker: A
text: People did offer to help, but I can't afford it, I need to know where everything is.

speaker: A
text: So I've been getting one hour of sleep a day.

speaker: A
text: So, you know, they've offered me a, you know, I return September 23rd to no home.

speaker: A
text: So they have some bungalows up near Canaan Doom Road, and one of them is a one bedroom,

speaker: A
text: so they're going to give me that until mid-November.

speaker: A
text: Because as soon as I get back, I'm only back a week, and then I go on my next tour here,

speaker: A
text: I go to Aspen, then Sedona, Chicago, and then St.

speaker: A
text: Louis. So I'll be gone that whole month, you know, of October.

speaker: A
text: So I'll have just two weeks in November to look for a place.

text: Q: You don't need a home.

speaker: A
text: A: Pardon?

speaker: Q
text: Q: You don't need a home, I'm just saying.

speaker: A
text: A: I need one about three months a year, you know, here in L.A.

speaker: A
text: So that one was a perfect one, my hot tub, everything.

speaker: A
text: And they've got to bury the hot tub.

speaker: A
text: Oh, no. I didn't know you needed a permit, but, you know, if I had gone for a permit for that hot tub then,

speaker: A
text: I would have lost the house ten years ago.

speaker: A
text: So that's when I built the hot tub.

speaker: Q
text: Q: You've been there ten years?

speaker: A
text: A: Eleven years.

speaker: A
text: Eleven years.

speaker: A
text: I thought I was going to be able to be there for my life.

text: Q: But you own the house, don't you?

speaker: A
text: A: No. I would have had a heart attack if I had to tear it down and it were mine.

speaker: A
text: Oh, yeah.

speaker: A
text: No, it belongs to Fred Segal.

speaker: A
text: So, you know, Fred Segal Clothing Store.

text: Q: So you were leasing it from him?

speaker: A
text: A: No, I'm renting.

speaker: A
text: Well, I was leasing on the yearly lease, but he said that I could, because he's on the diet and it saved his life

speaker: A
text: and changes his whole life.

speaker: A
text: He said that I could live there as long as I wanted, even after he's dead.

speaker: A
text: In fact, he made a deal when he rented the lease the place to the rehab center,

speaker: A
text: the clinic, that I stay there no matter what.

speaker: A
text: But the contract was on that house.

speaker: A
text: The house is gone.

speaker: A
text: That's it.

speaker: Q
text: Q: You take it pretty good.

speaker: A
text: A: What am I going to do about it?

speaker: A
text: I was upset for two hours.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Move on. Q: Time for a change.

speaker: A
text: A: Screw it.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Oh, wow.

speaker: A
text: A: I'm here so little, so it's okay.

speaker: A
text: One, two days at a time.

text: Q: Are you packing your stuff up?

speaker: Q
text: Where are you going to keep your stuff?

speaker: A
text: A: They have...

speaker: A
text: Fred on his part of the land that he didn't lease to them.

speaker: A
text: He has a small storage house.

speaker: A
text: He's going to put everything there for me.

speaker: A
text: And I've got three boxes that just has everything that I absolutely have to have.

speaker: A
text: So I'm not living in like a hotel.

speaker: A
text: Because that's basically, I live out of a suitcase for nine and a half months a year.

text: Q: Is

speaker: Q
text: that your plan, just to come back here a month at a time or something, three times a year?

speaker: A
text: A: Well, that's the way I'm doing it now.

speaker: A

speaker: A
text: Then going away again.

text: Q: And you're building a house in the Philippines, aren't you?

speaker: A
text: A: Not yet. It hasn't started.

speaker: A
text: It's all about to begin there.

speaker: A
text: Even though it's more remote and no roads into that area, no paved roads, and I have to cross three rivers.

speaker: A
text: We got caught in one of the rivers and almost got washed out into the ocean.

speaker: A
text: He and I were there last August.

speaker: A
text: But that's finally bought the property, finally went through in January.

speaker: A
text: So, I mean, because it's 618 meters up the mountain, and it's in forested land,

speaker: A
text: and they're very particular about everything.

speaker: A
text: So I had to get a permit and permission and have the town developers, the city of Puerto Princesa,

speaker: A
text: their engineers design the road because it's, I mean, this steep sometimes.

speaker: A
text: So they had to build a road which was a half a mile up the mountain to get to my property.

speaker: A
text: It took them four months to build it.

speaker: A
text: And I had to get permission to take down the trees and, you know.

speaker: Q
text: Q: So it's a process.

speaker: A
text: A: It was a heck of a process.

speaker: A
text: So then that was at the one end of the, the property is about a half a mile long.

speaker: A
text: It's a kilometer by almost 60%, two-thirds of a kilometer, you know, going back.

speaker: A
text: So it's a big piece of property.

speaker: A
text: The one in Thailand is only 34 acres, the one in the Philippines is 108 acres.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Only 34 acres.

speaker: A
text: A: And 108 acres is the one in the Philippines.

speaker: A
text: So they had to, I needed a lake built at the end where I was going to build the property because where it goes at that end,

speaker: A
text: at the north end of the property, there's a river that runs down and some big waterfalls on it, and that runs all year round.

speaker: A
text: And along the back of the property, there's a river that runs along the back and all along the other side.

speaker: A
text: So on three sides of the property there are lakes, the rivers.

speaker: A
text: Now the one on the north end, that is so big that that's government owned.

speaker: A
text: But my land goes right up to it.

speaker: A
text: The one that's behind it on the other side is on my property.

speaker: Q
text: Q: What made you choose the Philippines?

speaker: A
text: A: Because it was the most remote area I could get without getting into hostility.

speaker: A
text: If I was gone towards Indonesia or Malaysia, there's a lot of hostility towards white people.

speaker: A
text: I don't know, I didn't want to get into that.

speaker: A
text: Filipinos love white people, I mean Americans, I don't know why.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Do you they call you Joe?

speaker: A
text: A: No.

speaker: Q
text: Q: I was in Northern Philippines, they kept calling me Joe.

speaker: Q
text: From G.I.

speaker: Q
text: Joe? From the Vietnamese guys during the Vietnam War, a bunch of G.I.s.

speaker: A
text: A: But this is, if you look at the Philippines, you've got the big island Luzon here, where Manila is.

speaker: A
text: And then you've got all these other islands that go off over here, Samar, Leyte.

speaker: A
text: And then you have some fairly large islands there, which are Bajal, Cebu, Negros, and those are popular ones.

speaker: A
text: And then you have the big island, Mindanao here, and Samal, and all the little islands around that.

speaker: A
text: Then way over here, there's a long island, and that's Palawan, where I am.

speaker: A
text: Only 2% of the roads are paved.

speaker: A
text: The town I live in, there are 200 people, and they're all spread out over about five miles.

speaker: A
text: 200 people over a five-mile area, and they live off the land.

speaker: A
text: They have electricity one and a half hours a day, and that's it.

speaker: A
text: Because the city paid for a power thing for them to have electricity one and a half hours a day.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Do they fish?

speaker: A
text: A: Yeah, that's what they do.

speaker: A
text: It's right on the ocean there.

speaker: A
text: The place where I built my property was where the wind comes through, because it's all mountainous there.

speaker: A
text: I'm probably two-thirds of the way up the mountain, and all the way up to close to the top of that first peak.

speaker: A
text: Then it goes back about 12 miles to more mountains.

speaker: A
text: And that river runs 12 miles all the way down through my property.

speaker: A
text: I only hiked three miles back to see how it was all the way back there, and there's nothing back there but monkeys.

speaker: Q
text: Q: The drinking water must be good.

speaker: A
text: A: Oh, I drank right out of that stream.

speaker: Q
text: Q: That's what's nice.

speaker: A
text: A: They freaked out because they're told malaria.

speaker: A
text: They'll get malaria from it.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Oh my God.

speaker: A
text: A: I was bathing in it, you know.

speaker: A
text: They were freaked out.

speaker: A
text: They thought I was going to get malaria.

speaker: Q
text: Q: The people who live there, do they have wells?

speaker: A
text: A: They'll collect rain.

speaker: A
text: They won't drink it out of a stream.

speaker: A
text: They're indoctrinated to believe that they're going to get some disease.

speaker: A
text: They're going to get malaria, and it's a falsehood.

speaker: A
text: They believe that mosquitoes get malaria, too, and it's a joke.

speaker: A
text: It's ridiculous.

speaker: A
text: You know, a little bitty mosquito is going to bite you.

speaker: A
text: Now, think about this.

speaker: A
text: A mosquito is a female.

speaker: A
text: The only reason she drinks blood is to feed her offspring.

speaker: A
text: She doesn't want that blood contaminated.

speaker: A
text: She's not going to contaminate you when they bite you.

speaker: A
text: The proboscis goes in, and it bites as many cells as it can, so it creates a pool of blood.

speaker: A
text: She sucks it out.

speaker: A
text: No saliva involved in it or anything.

speaker: A
text: It's a whole ridiculous joke.

speaker: Q
text: Q: What about malaria?

speaker: Q
text: They say that's transmitted by...

speaker: A
text: A: That's what I'm saying.

speaker: A
text: That's what I'm talking about.

speaker: A
text: It's a lie.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Well, it must be a government-made lie.

speaker: A
text: A: Malaria comes from not eating enough protein and getting very sick in a humid climate.

speaker: A
text: And they only eat, like, 5%, 10% meats.

speaker: A
text: The healthier ones, they eat a lot because they're fishing.

speaker: A
text: Around where I bought my property, there's a lot.

speaker: A
text: But if you're one of the poorer people who has a big family, well, you know, they eat too much rice.

speaker: A
text: You know, 80% of the diet is rice.

speaker: A
text: The reason I was able to get the property, because they don't allow any foreigners over in that area,

speaker: A
text: was the second chief of this area, of this district, or what do they call it,

speaker: A
text: Barangay, he was supposed to show me the property the first time, and this was almost a year ago.

speaker: A
text: It was about a year ago this time.

speaker: A
text: February, I guess it was.

speaker: A
text: A year ago, February.

speaker: A
text: And I went there to see it, and he said, I'm sorry, I can't spend the whole day with you.

speaker: A
text: Two of my girls have malaria, and I have to take them to the hospital.

speaker: A
text: They're really sick.

speaker: A
text: So we had three languages to translate from, the native language to Tagalog, to English.

speaker: A
text: So by the time he got to translating me, I said 76% of the people who go into hospital for malaria die in the hospital.

speaker: A
text: Only 26%, 24% die if they don't go into the hospital.

speaker: A
text: So that was translated to him, and he thought for a few minutes, and he said, it's probably true.

speaker: A
text: Two of my girls, he had five girls.

speaker: A
text: He said, five years ago, two of my girls got malaria, and I took them to the hospital,

speaker: A
text: and they were dead in 24 hours, less than 24 hours.

speaker: A
text: I said, all you do is you take two ounces of lemon juice, two ounces of honey,

speaker: A
text: and mix it with six ounces of coconut water, and give them a tablespoon of that every hour for three days,

speaker: A
text: and then two tablespoons every two hours, or one tablespoon every two hours for another three days.

speaker: A
text: So he did that, he took me to the property, he spent the day there with me,

speaker: A
text: and he gave that to the kids, and they were fine, so that was why they decided to let me buy the property.

speaker: Q
text: Q: That's a great story.

speaker: A
text: A: They have a benefit for me being there, otherwise they wouldn't have sold it to me.

speaker: A
text: Of course, I had to have a corporation, where I own 40%, and the Filipinos have to own 60%.

speaker: A
text: So I got a taxi driver, my driver.

text: Q: You have a taxi driver?

speaker: A
text: A: A taxi driver, he's my foreman.

speaker: A
text: He used to be in farming, now he's a taxi driver, so whenever I'm there, he devotes all of his time to me.

speaker: Q
text: Q: He's very nice.

speaker: A
text: A: It's like $20 a day.

speaker: Q
text: Q: A bargain.

speaker: A
text: A: Yeah, tell me, $20 a day, and he'll take me everywhere, and he's mine for 24 hours.

speaker: A
text: I've taken cruises all around the island.

speaker: A
text: We had to rent a car, that was the most expensive, but I shipped an FJ Cruiser over there,

speaker: A
text: because I got a retirement visa, I was able to import a car.

speaker: A
text: So, an FJ Cruiser is like a cross between a Jeep and a Hummer, and it's a Toyota four-wheel drive.

speaker: A
text: It's a true off-road vehicle.

speaker: A
text: You can take those things and ride up the side of a cliff, you know, like this, and it won't turn over.

speaker: A
text: And because we got stuck in the river, you know, I needed something high, so it has six-inch lifts.

speaker: A
text: So for me to get up in it, I've got to climb up in it.

speaker: A
text: So it's an excellent, excellent car.

speaker: A
text: In fact, I have shots of a car being washed out in a river like we did with an FJ Cruiser that didn't have lifts on it.

speaker: A
text: And it finally hit a, you know, it was floating this much out of the thing.

speaker: A
text: You just see the top of the car only.

speaker: A
text: And then it hit a barge area, turned right on, drove right out.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Wow.

speaker: A
text: A: That's the car I wanted.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Perfect.

speaker: A
text: A: Yeah, so I've got that there.

speaker: A
text: It cost me a fortune, you know.

speaker: A
text: The FJ Cruiser, they don't import them there, but I found two of them only for sale in the Philippines.

speaker: A
text: They've been imported by Filipinos who had lived other places and returned and brought their cruisers with them.

speaker: A
text: And they wanted $60,000 for them.

speaker: A
text: So I bought it for $22,000 here, and it's worth $46,000.

speaker: A
text: It's a 2007.

speaker: A
text: And it cost me $13,000, almost $15,000 to import it.

speaker: A
text: So I still had to pay a fortune for it, but it's the vehicle that I want.

text: Q: How do you get the gas for it?

speaker: A
text: A: Well, there's gas stations.

speaker: Q
text: Q: I thought you were so remote.

speaker: A
text: A: Well, yeah, I have extra gas tanks, you know, to take with.

text: Q: What's your plan for the property?

text: I mean, are you going to do something about it?

text: A: Well, that property is just for me and relatives and friends.

speaker: A
text: But the one in Thailand will be a health spa.

text: It's even, you know, when I got...

text: There, I can own 49% of the corporation.

text: Q: Shareholders.

text: They have to be able to fulfill it.

speaker: A

speaker: A
text: So they really can't take it from me.

speaker: A
text: There's no way they can do it.

speaker: A
text: They couldn't afford to keep the land.

text: Q: Right.

text: A: So I made sure of that.

text: So that's the one I will make into a clinic eventually if my backers come in.

speaker: A
text: You know, that way.

text: I'm not going to build it myself.

speaker: A

speaker: A
text: It would get too much in the debt for me and I'm not going to do that.

speaker: A
text: It's a good idea.

text: Q: Is that up near Chiang Rai?

text: A: No, it's part of Khon Kaen province where Udon Thani is.

text: Q: It's on the eastern side, isn't it?

text: A: No, it's central.

speaker: A
text: So, Vinh Thien, Laos is here.

text: You drop down about 100 kilometers and there's Udon Thani.

speaker: A
text: Then you drop down about 130, 140 kilometers, maybe it's 200 kilometers, Khon Kaen.

speaker: A
text: And I'm off about 75 kilometers from that or more, probably 90 kilometers.

text: Q: So, how will you feed the fish in your pond?

speaker: A
text: A: Fish scraps.

speaker: A
text: I'll go collect them in town.

speaker: A
text: And then after I'm there, I just feed them any meat scraps that I have.

speaker: A
text: Just throw it into the pond and eat.

text: Q: Do you think that's as good as ocean fish?

speaker: A
text: A: Well, in Thailand I can't get the ocean fish because I'm dead center in the country.

speaker: A
text: So, no water around me except for a huge lake.

speaker: A
text: And there is a lake that's probably about 60 miles long.

speaker: A
text: And it looks like fingers if you see it.

speaker: A
text: It looks like a hand with all these fingers coming out of it.

speaker: A
text: And it's a pretty big lake.

speaker: A
text: It's probably 40 miles wide, 80, 90 miles long.

speaker: A
text: And I'm probably two miles from it walking distance.

speaker: A
text: But I'll take fish from there and scallops.

speaker: A
text: I mean, they have lots of like shrimp, you know, freshwater prawns.

speaker: A
text: And I'll put those in my fish pond and build my aquarium that I will eat from.

speaker: A
text: So I mainly eat fish, you know, freshwater fish there.

speaker: A
text: But when I'm in Palawan, you know, the place where I cut the area for a house is overlooking.

speaker: A
text: I've got a panoramic view of the ocean and the mountains.

speaker: A
text: That's gorgeous.

speaker: A
text: So that's only, you know, about a mile down to the ocean from there.

speaker: A
text: And I do have a big old dirt bike and now the FJ Cruiser to get around there.

speaker: A
text: So I can go down fishing anytime I want.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Are there animals on Palawan?

speaker: A
text: A: There's a dairy that's a government dairy that was a test dairy that was started.

speaker: A
text: New Zealand funded it.

speaker: A
text: Now they fund it, but there's, I get all the milk that they have.

speaker: A
text: They only have two milking cows, you know, but they're Holsteins.

speaker: A
text: So there's very little fat, very little cream in them.

speaker: A
text: So they're V2 cows, you know, A2s I mean, not A1s.

speaker: A
text: So the milk, even though it's nourishing, it's not as nourishing as I would like.

speaker: A
text: So I will find some, and there are on different islands, like on Samal Island.

speaker: A
text: There's 7,107 islands in the Philippines.

speaker: A
text: I will do a lot of island hopping to see all of it.

speaker: A
text: But I found a big dairy on Samal Island, which is part of Mindanao.

speaker: A
text: And they've got a pretty big dairy there, and they have jerseys.

speaker: A
text: So I will either buy it from them or...

speaker: Q
text: Q: Can you buy a couple cows?

speaker: A
text: A: Yeah, I can buy a couple cows.

speaker: A
text: I just have to put the fence up.

speaker: Q
text: Q: Would you be able to get enough cream in a tropical environment from the cows?

speaker: A
text: A: Yeah, it's there that when you have a cow in the tropics, the vitamin D in it keeps it homogenized.

speaker: A
text: So it doesn't separate the same.

speaker: A
text: But I don't need it to separate in the tropics because I don't need...

speaker: A
text: If you eat butter there, which I take with me, it causes a lot more perspiration and heat, body heat.

speaker: A
text: I like the heat, so it doesn't bother me.

speaker: A
text: But people look at me dripping wet, and they say, Oh my God, are you okay?

speaker: A
text: I say, I love it.

speaker: A
text: But if you have the cream and milk, you don't perspire as much.

speaker: A
text: Butter will make you perspire profusely.

speaker: A
text: So I wouldn't make butter there.

speaker: A
text: I would just have rich, creamy milk.

speaker: Q
text: Q: So people coming in wouldn't be getting butter at the clinic?

speaker: A
text: A: No. Well, I would probably import some or somehow make some.

speaker: A
text: Definitely, I would have to have butter for some sick people.

speaker: A
text: I would find a way, put a little bit of lemon or something in it to separate it.

speaker: A
text: To make sure it's separated.

speaker: Q
text: Q: So there's really no way to get butter in a tropical place from a tropical farm?

speaker: A
text: A: Yeah, there is.

speaker: A
text: You just have to have a certain kind of cattle.

speaker: A
text: And they have to eat...

speaker: A
text: You have to grow something that they'll produce more fat.

speaker: A
text: When they're eating the regular grasses there, no matter what it is, they're not going to produce much fat.

text: Q: What are you hoping to achieve with your health spa?

speaker: A
text: A: Help people get well.

speaker: A
text: That's all.

speaker: A
text: Because there's a lot of people who need daily help.

speaker: A
text: And I'm not set up for that, and I've had a lot of people ask me for that over the years.

speaker: A
text: People with cancer, MS, serious problems that could get well fast if I were there to help them.

speaker: A
text: And so I would be for that.

text: Q: Are you going to be doing any training when you set up your health spa?

text: A: Well, if I set that up, I will definitely do training.
